speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly where your neck and arm pain is located, and which specific fingers or areas are experiencing the tingling sensations?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The bilateral nature of your symptoms, combined with your history of diabetes and prior trauma, raises concern for cervical myelopathy or severe stenosis. Do you experience any difficulty with balance, walking, or fine motor tasks like buttoning shirts?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of upper and lower motor neuron signs, specifically fasciculations and weakness with absent reflexes, is highly suggestive of motor neuron disease. Do you have any difficulty swallowing, speaking, or breathing?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, history of a motor vehicle accident 3 years prior. Social history: 7 sexual partners, uses condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absent reflexes and fasciculations are a critical combination that helps narrow the differential significantly. Do you have any numbness or loss of sensation in your hands, or is the issue purely motor weakness?

speaker: Patient
text: Oriented to time, place, and person. Vital signs within normal limits.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of sensory loss despite significant weakness and fasciculations strongly points toward a pure motor neuron pathology rather than a root or cord compression. Given the asymmetric weakness, fasciculations, and absent reflexes, I am highly suspicious of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS). I will request an EMG to confirm the presence of widespread denervation and reinnervation. REQUEST TEST: Electromyography (EMG) and Nerve Conduction Studies.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal EMG and nerve conduction studies effectively rule out ALS and peripheral neuropathy, shifting the focus back to the cervical spine given the history of trauma and neck pain. I need to visualize the structural integrity of the cervical cord to assess for compression or myelopathy. REQUEST TEST: MRI of the Cervical Spine

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of a cervical syrinx perfectly explains your combination of burning pain, segmental weakness, and fasciculations, a condition known as Syringomyelia. This cavity in the spinal cord is likely compressing the anterior horn cells, leading to the lower motor neuron signs we observed.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia
